full_judgment:
9. The management contested the case by filing written statement contending that the, case so filed was barred by limitation, that the case was not maintainable since the first party (respondent No.3 herein) was never a worker, that the first party was in the employment of the management as Secretary cum Accountant and that the said post is an Administrative post as well as Managerial and, as such, the first party did not come within the definition of worker as given in the Act of 1936 as well as in the Act of 1965, that in spite of repeated directions to the first party to join his duties he having not joined the management brought to end his service on and from 31-10-1987 and, as such, the first party was not entitled to any amount on any account from the Management. 

 10. The Labour Court on consideration of the materials placed before it by the parties in support of their respective case and that on consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary, on the findings that the first party was a worker in the employment of the second party and that his service was terminated by the management, that the case so filed was not barred by limitation, the case was maintainable, that the first party was entitled to termination benefits and thereupon awarded Taka 1,34,135.00 as termination benefits to the worker as well as an amount of Taka 500.00 as compensatory cost as against the Management. 

 11. The Management being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment of the Labour Court went on appeal before the Labour Appellate Tribunal. The Labour Appellate Tribunal on consideration of the materials on record allowed the appeal upon concurring with the findings and decisions of the Labour Court as to that the first party was a worker, that he was entitled to termination benefits as provided in section 19(1) of the Act of 1965, that the case so filed by the first party before the Labour Court was not barred by limitation and that the same was maintainable under section 15(2) of the Act of 1936 and thereupon allowed the appeal in part upon reducing the termination benefits to Taka 84,770.00 from Taka 1,34,135.00. 

 15. Learned Advocate for the respondent No.3 of both the Writ Petitions submits that any amount payable to a worker on termination of his   employment being wages as defined in section 2(vi)   of the Act of 1936 and that the said termination   benefits having not been paid the Labour Court, as   well as the Labour Appellate Tribunal, had quite   legally awarded the same as per provisions of  sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 15 of the Act of   1936, that mere designation does not take a person   out of the definition of 'worker' given in section 2(v)   of the Act of 1965 in the absence of it being  established by the management that the said person  discharged duties and performed functions of  administrative or managerial nature or that being   employed in supervisory capacity discharged duties   mainly of managerial or administrative nature, the Labour Court as well as the Labour Appellate   Tribunal upon due consideration of the materials  placed by the respondent No.3 in support of his   claim and that by the petitioner herein in support of   the contention that respondent No.3 was not a   worker having had held that the respondent No.3 (in   both the writ petitions) was a worker in the   employment of the managements (petitioners herein)   and that no illegality of any kind having been  committed in arriving at the finding that the  respondent No.3 was a worker in the employment of  the managements that same is not liable to be   interfered with by this court in exercise of the  jurisdiction in certiorari, that the Labour Court, as   well as Labour Appellate Tribunals was quite legal  in holding that the application filed under section 15   (2) of the Act of 1936 was quite maintainable and   that the same was also not barred by limitation.
